searchText: We had great results on non-EOF JIT FWIW here! https://github.com/paradigmxyz/revmc Strong NACK from our side on EVM64. I wish that the VM instructions ever were the bottleneck on performance, but it's not. Based on your experience, do you think RISC-V will also be of no use (for addressing the bottleneck on performance) or is it totally different? We actually had previously some problems with this approach of JIT, because from what I know LLVM/Cranelift aren't one-pass. So JIT bombs are now possible! (That's why Wasm is also problematic JITing untrusted code.) Is the benchmarking based on runtime or runtime+compiletime? Do you believe it would be safe and feasible to decrease the slot time as part of Glamsterdam if EIP-7886 is implemented? There are real (eg. mev reduction, UX improvement, faster time to finality & better L2 intraop) and narrative benefits that slot time decreases address better than gas limit increases. Shorter Slot Times
